node_name: WordNet lexical-semantic synsets for concept representation
case_title: A combined approach for improving humanoid robots autonomous cognitive capabilities
evidence_statement: WordNet is a dictionary containing lexical-semantic connections between abstract concepts
object_definition: The fundamental unit is a synset, i.e., a set of terms having the same meaning; each synset represents a concept in WordNet

node_name: General Knowledge Base (GKB) ontological structure
case_title: A combined approach for improving humanoid robots autonomous cognitive capabilities
evidence_statement: The knowledge base is called general since it has been implemented starting from a high-level ontological model acting as overarching ontology, in turn defined following the structure of WordNet
object_definition: A knowledge base providing a means for information to be collected, organized, shared, searched and utilized; contains general concepts and multimedia representations from WordNet and ImageNet

node_name: Local Knowledge Base (LKB) for robot-specific concept instantiation
case_title: A combined approach for improving humanoid robots autonomous cognitive capabilities
evidence_statement: Each artificial system is provided with its own local knowledge base (LKB), which keeps the reference with the general knowledge base, but it is free to evolve on its own by adding new unknown concepts
object_definition: A localized knowledge store that maintains reference to GKB while allowing autonomous evolution and addition of new concepts

node_name: GHSOM horizontal growth threshold parameter (τ1)
case_title: A combined approach for improving humanoid robots autonomous cognitive capabilities
evidence_statement: The first parameter, τ₁, is used in the stopping criterion for the growth of a single map in the architecture
object_definition: Used in Eq.2 (MQE_map_i < τ₁ · qej) to control individual map growth; example: τ₁ = 0.1 means map error must be less than one-tenth of father neuron's error

node_name: GHSOM vertical growth threshold parameter (τ2)
case_title: A combined approach for improving humanoid robots autonomous cognitive capabilities
evidence_statement: The second parameter, τ₂, is used to specify the minimum quality of data representation of each unit as a fraction of the quantization error of the zero unit
object_definition: Used in Eq.3 (qei < τ₂ · qe0) to control vertical growth; directly influences GHSOM depth

node_name: Wu-Palmer semantic similarity distance metric
case_title: A combined approach for improving humanoid robots autonomous cognitive capabilities
evidence_statement: The Wu-Palmer similarity is a measure already normalized in the range [0, 1]
object_definition: A semantic similarity measure used in fitness function; inverse calculated as (1 - Wu-Palmer)

node_name: Fixed topology size constraint of classical SOM
case_title: A combined approach for improving humanoid robots autonomous cognitive capabilities
evidence_statement: Having a fixed size of the map forces the definition of clusters which could become at least not appropriate, or even meaningless, when new knowledge is added
object_definition: SOM's predetermined number of neurons cannot adapt to new knowledge; size parameter often determined by experiments and based on available data

node_name: Non-hierarchical flat structure constraint of classical SOM
case_title: A combined approach for improving humanoid robots autonomous cognitive capabilities
evidence_statement: The flatness of the map does not allow to organize data hierarchically
object_definition: Lack of hierarchical organization in SOM, limiting cognitive processes that rely on semantic hierarchies (as documented in Brooks' subsumption architectures)

node_name: Inflexible monolithic structure of ontologies
case_title: A combined approach for improving humanoid robots autonomous cognitive capabilities
evidence_statement: Ontologies reflect a fundamentally monolithic view of knowledge, i.e., they are too rigid and cannot easily manage exceptions and shades of knowledge
object_definition: Inflexibility of ontologies to handle exceptions, nuances, and dynamic knowledge evolution; contrast with flexibility and interpretability requirements

node_name: Pepper humanoid robot platform (knowledge learner)

evidence_statement: The robot starts the exploration of the environment and analyzes the objects he finds on his way
